tbl_description: 'Final Underway Data' CSV, UTC confirmed by column name (DATE_TIME_UTC/DATE_UTC/TIME_UTC). 18 cruises 2010-2016, the largest retrievable group. Three header widths occur: the canonical 12 columns; an 11-column form without Flowmeter_LPM (1402SH, 1607OS); and 1004MF, whose header omits Longitude_W although the data carries the column — repaired at read time by inserting the name, since reading it as-published shifts every field after latitude by one.

'Final Underway Data' as .xlsx (CC{YYMM}UW_1MinData.xlsx), 22 cruises 2016-2022, ~1-minute resolution. NOT three fixed schemas: the 22 files carry 50+ distinct column names with no two eras identical (1-3 TSG units, optional bottom depth / pH / oxygen-saturation / underway-DIC packages, and spelling variants AtmPres~AtmPress, TSGTemp~TSG_Temp). Columns are therefore mapped BY NAME from a single union dictionary rather than by matching a file to a schema variant, and any unmapped column is reported rather than dropped.

Header-less 9-column CSV ({cruise}{SHIP}10mindata.csv), 8 cruises 2004-2005, ~10-minute resolution. Column identity is positional and unconfirmed (mets_01): date YYYYMMDD, time HHMMSS, an integer counter that equals seconds-since-midnight in some cruises but not others, lat, lon, temperature, salinity, and two columns that are NaN throughout every file inspected. The separately-linked {cruise}_SCIMS.txt files of the same era return 403 and are not retrievable (mets_11).

'Raw Underway Data' for 1207OS (2012), shipped as a zip containing two date-split txt files plus Underway_explantation.docx. Header-less: date MM/DD/YYYY, time HH:MM:SS.sss, temperature, conductivity, salinity from a single Seabird TSG 45. No lat/lon at all, so geom/grid_key stay NULL for this cruise (mets_16). Records are separated by blank lines.

0903JD (2009), shipped as a zip containing one tab-separated txt with a real header (DATE_PST/TIME_PST/LA/LO/ST/SA/CAL_T/CAL_S). Dates are D-Mon-YY (e.g. 7-Mar-09), not numeric. Pacific time is explicit in the column names; the cruise ran 7-24 Mar 2009, entirely in standard time, so a fixed -8:00 is correct here — the general convention is still unconfirmed (mets_19).

'Underway Data - SCS' ({cruise}_SCS.txt, 2006-2008). Linked on the underway page for 9 cruises but every request returns 403 Forbidden, so no example has ever been retrieved and the schema is unknown. Out of scope until the files are served (mets_12); the ingest reports them as linked-but-unavailable rather than silently skipping them.
